scope: Kayenta Obsession second-edition base/core, standard 16-round 2–4-player multiplayer with base objectives; Universal Rules Compendium 2025-12-17 plus Corrigendum 1.0 2026-10-06; marked expansions, optional variants and alternate modes excluded.
conclusion: No material inaccurate claim or important omission was found within the requested scope. The independently checked supplemental source supports the reputation-objective clarification.

checked_claims.assessment: Base/core 2–4-player standard game; 16 track spaces mean 12 ordinary turns, and courtship has no turns or ongoing effects. Marked expansion/optional material is excluded. Full seasonal market refresh is the selected standard.
source_refs: Universal Rules Compendium pp.8–12, 16, 21, 23; Appendix legends pp.80, 86, 106

checked_claims.assessment: Family draft starts left of first player; reputation, five starting servants/tiles, family bonuses, starter guest reintegration, five objectives, servant supply, monument selection, six distinct initial market spaces and initial theme/Fairchild setup agree.
Standard track events are Village Fair 3/9, objectives 6, Builders’ Holiday 11, National Holiday 14 and courtship 4/8/12/16.
source_refs: Universal Rules Compendium pp.12 (standard board illustration), 17

checked_claims.assessment: Service rotation and pass recovery order, exact attendee types/counts, service, mandatory favours with positive-before-negative ordering, purchases, cleanup and ordinary-round advancement agree. Hiring on passing is excluded as optional for base.

Screening fixes reputation level at end of step 2; later special actions do not invalidate attendance. Limits 1.1–7.5, minimum protection, maximum overflow handling and Borrow Money/Service Help/Refresh Market costs and repetition limits agree.
Public money, unlimited supply, no transfers, full payment of money penalties with borrowing when possible, and minimum floor for reputation penalties agree.

Unique/common definitions, housekeeper/Brushing Room restrictions, underbutler substitutions, Butler’s Room hiring/recruiting, Butler’s Pantry acquisition into Expended Service and Servants’ Quarters tile ability agree.

Hand/discard ownership, no family dismissal, screening/dismissal destinations and visibility, unsavoury classification, family favours/VP, Fairchild requirements/favours/VP and base gossip effects agree.
Mandatory normal upgrades, ongoing-only restrictions, hybrid initial side/flipping/category, monuments and suite conversion income timing, Barn and Servants’ Hall agree.

Heritage/Queen’s/Lionheart staffing, single-guest count, doubling and destinations agree. Private Study, Main Library, South Lawn and standard West Terrace claims agree. Other unmarked base tile entries were read for material omissions.
source_refs: Universal Rules Compendium pp.79, 86–104; especially pp.93, 95–96, 99, 101, 104

checked_claims.assessment: Price modifiers/minimum, one-tile total limit, no duplicate acquisition, stacking/sliding/refill sorting, Service/PR1 Reserve opening, Largest Wine Cellar exception, all Reserve tiles available and refresh isolation agree.

Builders’ Holiday/Market Purchase share a single unchanged market and fixed existing prices before refill; no refresh between purchases. Multiple VP refreshes and separate paid/pass refresh methods are supported.
source_refs: Universal Rules Compendium p.40, Builders’ Holiday; p.78, Special Actions FAQ; p.105, Market Purchase/Market Refresh

checked_claims.assessment: Normal seven objectives/four discards/three retained, additional-objective retention, bottom-deck destinations, no upgrade requirement, own-turn/immediate/final VP usage and all eleven VP benefit entries agree.

Fairchild return, seasonal category scoring including negative VP, ties, objective discard, seasonal upkeep order, cumulative final theme scoring/repeated categories, reputation-level final courtship tie break, final benefits and all seven final VP sources/tiebreakers agree.

All thirty base objective types and their base-specific values/requirements were checked against entries labelled Base, including common-only basic servants, all-servant total objective, monument/category/hybrid handling and tile ownership without upgrades.
Maximum level/Max counter completion is supported by the official localized base rulebook example; Max is standard level 7. This source was used only for that unchanged objective, not seasonal flow.
source_refs: Super Meeple official French base rulebook p.7 (Max counter definition), p.14 (3. PV des cartes Objectif and depicted Reputation Bonus card)
Universal Rules Compendium p.111, Reputation Bonus

source_review.full_relevant_text_read: Universal Rules Compendium pp.8–12, 16–24, 26–30, 35–42, 76–85, 86–105 and all objective entries pp.106–111; marked expansion-only entries were recognized and excluded from the base verdict. Corrigendum pp.1–2 reviewed.
source_review.pdf_checks: Direct PDF inspection included standard Alderley Hall board illustration on compendium p.12, direct text extraction of both corrigendum pages, and the actual objective/scoring example illustrations on official French rulebook p.14. Supplemental French pp.7 and 14 text read.
source_review.supplemental_source_limit: Only the maximum-level reputation objective clarification was taken from the Super Meeple base rulebook. No older seasonal flow was imported.

independence_statement: This was a fresh source audit of the supplied summary snapshot. I did not read questions, answer keys, reader answers, grades, prior audits or other QA artifacts. I did not communicate with readers, edit the summary or author repairs. I read only the authorized summary and primary-source material, plus temporary image extractions made from the authorized PDFs. The verdict was determined from those sources without assuming a pass.
